CELL BIOLOGY AND CELLULAR STRUCTURE

CELL THEORY AND CELL CLASSIFICATION
The Cell Theory states that all living organisms are composed of one or more cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells through cell division.
Prokaryotic cells are primitive cellular structures that lack a membrane-enclosed nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Eukaryotic cells are advanced cellular structures characterized by a distinct membrane-bound nucleus and specialized cytoplasmic organelles.

PLASMA MEMBRANE AND CYTOPLASMIC ORGANELLES
The Plasma Membrane is a selectively permeable biological barrier described by the Fluid Mosaic Model, consisting of a phospholipid bilayer with embedded transport proteins.
The Endoplasmic Reticulum is a continuous network of membranous tubules; rough endoplasmic reticulum contains bound ribosomes for protein synthesis, whereas smooth endoplasmic reticulum synthesizes lipids.
The Golgi Apparatus consists of flattened cisternae that function in sorting, packaging, and chemical modification of proteins for intracellular delivery or cellular secretion.
Mitochondria are double-membraned cellular organelles that serve as the biochemical powerhouses of the eukaryotic cell, producing adenosine triphosphate through oxidative phosphorylation.
Ribosomes are dense non-membrane bound ribonucleoprotein granules that translate messenger RNA into polypeptide chains.
Lysosomes are acidic membrane-bound digestive vesicles containing hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular catabolism.

THE CELL NUCLEUS AND GENETIC ARCHITECTURE
The Nucleus is the principal regulatory organelle enclosing eukaryotic genetic material within a double-layered nuclear envelope.
Chromatin is an organized nucleoprotein complex composed of deoxyribonucleic acid and basic histone proteins that condenses into chromosomes during mitotic cell division.
The Nucleolus is a dense subnuclear structure responsible for the biogenesis of ribosomal RNA.
